comparator.route: Dutch-taught Psychology with Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 regulations and exact Dutch prospectus establish 180 EC. The first year contains twelve required 5 EC courses. The later years contain nine required 5 EC courses and the 15 EC Bachelor Project. At least 20 EC of specialisation and enough Psychology electives to reach 30 EC are required, alongside 30 EC of open study in this illustration. Both selected specialisation courses require passing all first-year courses. The standard Bachelor Project requires passing year one and Multivariate Data Analysis. Students work in a research team and are assessed on a research article, presentation and the research and collaboration process.

comparatorRouteSelection.route: Dutch-taught Psychology with Cognitive Neuroscience and Social Psychology in Organisations
comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Psychology bachelor. The programme requires specialisation choices but is explicitly broad. Selecting one cognitive-neuroscience course and one social-organisational course preserves that cross-domain identity and avoids presenting a narrow clinical, cognitive or organisational profile as the whole programme. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad option covers development, clinical and social psychology, cognition and behavioral methods. The brain option adds biological mechanisms, laboratory work and computation. The organizational option adds applied leadership, consumer behavior and organizational research. The clinical and development/trauma interests are visible within the broad option; separate professional clinical or specialist trauma curricula would overstate the depth of the available sequence.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both examine attitudes, groups and social influence. Leiden also introduces organizational psychology in this unit.
Both examine development. UCR follows development across the lifespan, while Leiden also addresses educational psychology.
Leiden requires a separate history of psychology course.
This plan reserves 10 EC for Psychology electives.
Leiden requires an introductory survey of psychology. UCR’s gateway combines psychological and neuroscience foundations.
Both introduce neural and psychological explanations of behavior. UCR combines this with broader psychological foundations.
Both introduce clinical and mental-health questions. UCR focuses on psychopathology and the biopsychosocial context of mental health.
Both introduce psychological assessment. UCR also surveys psychotherapy approaches.
Both study neural mechanisms of cognition. UCR focuses on perception and action, while Leiden’s specialisation covers a wider range of topics and methods.
Both study attention, memory and other cognitive processes. UCR emphasizes their neural and experimental foundations.
Leiden requires a course on stress, health and illness. UCR addresses related topics within medical and health psychology.
Leiden requires a separate developmental psychopathology course. UCR studies development and psychopathology in broader courses.
Leiden requires a separate consciousness course.
Both examine motivation, group processes and organizational culture. UCR applies these ideas to leadership and organizational behavior.
Leiden requires a separate unit in interpersonal professional skills for psychology.
Leiden requires a separate Group Dynamics course. UCR addresses group processes in social psychology and leadership.
Both teach statistical inference in psychological research. UCR combines statistics with experimental design.
Both develop critical evaluation of research. UCR focuses on systematic reviews and meta-analysis.
Both develop empirical research design and statistical analysis. UCR includes a group research project.
Leiden requires a separate course in psychological measurement and test quality.
Leiden requires a psychology course in multivariate methods. UCR offers econometric modeling in two options.
Leiden requires a 15 EC psychology research project. UCR’s optional independent research is outside the scheduled 180 EC.
Leiden’s tutorial develops academic skills for psychology. UCR develops general academic skills in Personal & Professional Development.
Leiden requires an experimental and correlational research course. UCR teaches experimental design and applied statistics within its methods sequence.
Leiden requires a psychology-specific career planning unit.
This plan reserves 30 EC for open study.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s Psychology bachelor studies behavior, cognition, development and mental health. Students learn psychological research methods, take specialisation courses and complete a supervised research project. This comparison uses the Dutch-taught route.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR options emphasize broad psychology and research, brain and cognition, or psychology and organizations. Each brings together psychology and complementary disciplines. Leiden provides a more extensive sequence of psychology-specific measurement and professional skills.
